clue.text: Free from deception, having sorted out bad issue

indicators.note: letters that are sorted out are put into a new order, so the words bad issue get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets the record straight after tidying up a botched magazine edition.
explanation.definitionFit: To disabuse someone is to rid them of a mistaken belief, freeing them from deception.

clue.text: Indulged, oddly, so do nothing

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions of the word Indulged: first, third, fifth, seventh

explanation.surface: Having been pampered, someone decides to laze about.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to pass time without working, a verb synonym for doing nothing.

clue.text: Retriever, for example, raised with intelligence to bring bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a retriever is a breed of dog
wit means intelligence or quick thinking

explanation.surface: A gun dog trained to be clever is used to fetch shot game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The godwit is a long-billed wading bird of shores and marshes.

clue.text: Sign of distress of female quickly disappears

parts.note: tears are a visible sign of being upset
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's upset passes off rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tears off rushes away at speed, an informal idiom for hurrying off.

clue.text: Part of engine that's minute in small train set, possibly

indicators.note: the letter for minute is placed inside the string of letters built from the other pieces

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to train someone is to teach them

indicators.note: possibly signals the word set may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A model railway component is found among the pieces of a tiny toy train set.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam chest is the chamber on a steam engine that feeds steam to the cylinders.

clue.text: Plants free of insects? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase's synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: bugless would mean having no bugs, that is free of insects

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether some greenery is pest-free, and the answer is almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugles are low creeping plants of the mint family, genus Ajuga, with blue flower spikes.

clue.text: It might come from robins, holding one note, then another

definitions.text: It might come from robins, holding one note, then another

parts.words: It might come from robins, holding one note, then another
parts.note: describes what a garden bird produces: a sustained note followed by a different one, the music of the hedgerow

explanation.definitionFit: Robins and other birds produce melodic calls made of successive notes, which is their characteristic music.

clue.text: Animal in Highlands turned up beside Scott's hero

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is written upwards, reversing it

parts.note: the stag, a male red deer, is the emblematic beast of the Scottish Highlands
by means beside or next to

explanation.surface: A Highland deer stands next to a Scottish author's protagonist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scott' looks like Walter Scott given the Highlands, but it is F. Scott Fitzgerald, author of The Great Gatsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the title character of F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel, so the protagonist of that author.

clue.text: Tea? Go to cafe, say

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: rearrange the letters of the first word, with out as the anagram signal, and you produce this clue word

explanation.surface: Fancy a cuppa? Let's head to a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: treat the answer as wordplay, with 'out' signalling an anagram of EAT, and it yields TEA, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining out means having a meal at a restaurant or cafe rather than at home, of which a cafe visit is an example.

clue.text: Gifted geniuses are very exceptional to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with takes the opening letter of each of the four words that precede it

explanation.surface: A remark that talented geniuses stand out from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted as a past tense verb means presented as a present, the same as handed over freely.

clue.text: Fashion a better law that's important for operating well

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder is these three words, all their letters used

explanation.surface: A call to draft improved legislation that helps things run smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating well' looks like running efficiently, but it means a working well for drawing water.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground level of saturated ground determines whether a sunk well yields water, so it matters for a working well.

clue.text: Crude alcohol, good with pickled trout

indicators.note: pickled suggests something mixed up or preserved in a jumble, rearranging the letters of trout

explanation.surface: A rough spirit served alongside fish preserved in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a slang term for cheap, harsh liquor that upsets the stomach.

clue.text: Fish bled disastrously between banks

indicators.note: between puts the rearranged letters into the middle of the synonym for banks

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it, so banks means relies

indicators.note: disastrously means badly gone wrong, so the letters of bled are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fish bleeds badly on the river's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-bellied fish such as the red-bellied piranha or dace are known by this name.

clue.text: Piece of furniture cook rearranged in HQ

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for headquarters

parts.note: a headquarters is a base

indicators.note: rearranged signals that the letters of cook are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A chef moved around the offices of a company's head office.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of shelves for holding volumes is a standard household furnishing.

clue.text: Some friend offers to complete some knitting, say

indicators.note: some of the words friend offers supplies a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A friend volunteers to finish off a bit of crochet.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish a piece of knitting by casting off the final stitches is a phrasal verb sense.

clue.text: How to film, mostly badly, and behave irresponsibly towards

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, scrambling them
mostly means all but the last letter of the word film is used

explanation.surface: An instruction guide on how to shoot a movie, largely done poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mess about with something or treat it carelessly is a phrasal verb meaning to trifle.

clue.text: Switch position in front of goal and commit foul

parts.note: off is one of the two positions of a switch
an end can mean an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A footballer standing offside near the goal commits a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress or break a rule is the sense here, equivalent to committing an offence.

clue.text: Dickensian character in dull, laborious work

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Charles Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure trapped in dreary, toilsome employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, menial and tedious labour is a near synonym for toil.

clue.text: They cut into ice to get fish

definitions.meaning: blades worn on boots for gliding slice the frozen surface
flat cartilaginous sea fish related to rays

explanation.surface: Blades bite into a frozen pond to catch something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ice blades and a kind of flat ray-like fish.

clue.text: Medical records that doctor wrote up for consultant

definitions.text: Medical records that doctor wrote up for consultant

parts.words: Medical records that doctor wrote up for consultant
parts.note: describes a file of patient histories written up by a physician for a senior specialist

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's record of individual patients and their treatment is a case record volume.

clue.text: A maximum possible speed in a vehicle? You can count on it

indicators.note: in places the first word and the speed letter inside the vehicle phrase

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle, giving A BUS
taken as written
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light, the fastest anything can travel

explanation.surface: A question about the top speed reachable by a car or coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires is used for calculating, so one literally counts on it.

clue.text: Teacher returned carrying gallon — cheap hooch

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds the gallon letter inside it
returned means the word for teacher is written backwards

parts.note: a tutor is a private teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster comes back with a large container of cheap spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior, harsh liquor is slang for poor quality alcohol.

clue.text: Full of enthusiasm, runs a syndicate

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a ring is a group working together, like a cartel or syndicate

explanation.surface: An eager entrepreneur manages a business consortium.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager and keen to start, as in itching to go, is the adjectival sense.

clue.text: The drink some diners prefer still

definitions.text: The drink some diners prefer still

parts.words: The drink some diners prefer still
parts.note: describes the bottled beverage served with a meal, which some people order without bubbles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'even now', but it means non-sparkling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled mineral water served at meals comes either sparkling or non-carbonated.

clue.text: Brilliant star trapped in compulsive gambling

indicators.note: trapped in means the letters sit inside the words compulsive gambling

explanation.surface: A celebrity is caught up in a betting addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant star' looks like a celebrity, but it is the bright star in Lyra.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, among the brightest in the night sky.

clue.text: British in contest felt atmosphere

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the verb for compete

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.surface: A British competitor sensed the mood at the event.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibe is the mood or feeling one senses about a place, slang for ambience.

clue.text: At mealtime excel every other character in robust repast

indicators.note: every other character in takes alternate letters of robust repast, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone surpasses everyone at dinner with a hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume more food than someone else is to beat them at eating.

clue.text: Stupidly bring in obnoxious person for a lark, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the anagrammed letters inside the word for an obnoxious person

parts.note: sod is British slang for an unpleasant person

indicators.note: stupidly suggests the letters are arranged foolishly, scrambling bring

explanation.surface: Foolishly involving a nasty piece of work just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a lark' looks like 'for fun', but a lark is the example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is an example of a singing bird, hence 'perhaps'.
